full_text:
Isaac of Mosul, the chief musician of Harun al-Rashid, was dining at the mansion of a wealthy textile merchant in Baghdad. While all the guests praised Isaac’s fame, an elderly, austere merchant named Abu Salih sat with crossed arms, declaring with contempt: 'Music is a frivolous waste of time; it is nothing but the scraping of gut strings against wood. It can neither weave cloth, nor build houses, nor soften a hard heart!'

The other guests were scandalized by the insult, but Isaac smiled with serene confidence. 'Brother,' said Isaac gently, 'will you grant me five minutes of your ear before you condemn my art?'

The old merchant grumbled: 'Play if you must; you will not stir a single hair on my beard.'

Isaac took his cedarwood lute, tightened the silk pegs, and touched the strings. At first, he played a brisk, martial rhythm with sharp chords; the old merchant’s foot tapped unconsciously upon the carpet.

Next, Isaac modulated into a playful, lively dance melody; the merchant’s stern lips twitched, and a faint smile appeared in his eyes.

Finally, Isaac tuned the lowest string to the ancient mode of Iraq, singing a soft, soulful ballad of the Euphrates orchards, of childhood homes left behind, and of mothers singing by the cradle in the dusk of summer. His voice was like a gentle river of pure memory and sorrow.

The guests held their breath. Isaac glanced up and saw tears streaming down Abu Salih's wrinkled cheeks! The old merchant threw his arms around the musician, weeping: 'Forgive me, master! You have not played upon wood; you have opened the locked chamber of my childhood memories and brought my mother’s voice back to my ears.'

The merchant gifted Isaac a robe of gold brocade, learning that art is not a frivolous diversion, but the key that unlocks the deepest sanctuary of the human soul.
moral: The true power of music is a universal language that can unlock the most stubborn and guarded heart. [ZH]
